evidence.title: Holder's history of the Rylands set
evidence.summary: Project under Ilantai, a pupil of Castiglione, began 1781 and was done by February 1787. This set was sent by Bourgeois to Delatour, probably in 1786; its condition suggests proofs before the presentation of 1787. Sheets later mounted on French paper and bound; bought by Mrs Rylands from the Earl of Crawford in 1901.

evidence.title: Bourgeois on his set and on the colouring; Delatour on its arrival
evidence.excerpt_other: l'autre avoit commencé à mettre en couleur la première planche, mais il tomba malade et n'acheva pas. J'ai mis son esquisse, toute imparfaite qu'elle est, dans la caisse
evidence.summary: Two pupils of Castiglione got Bourgeois a set: one drew the general plan and positions of the buildings, the other began colouring the first plate. Delatour says the sending reached him at the end of 1787 and had certainly left Peking from 1785, against the holder's 'probably 1786'. E0462 has the first part of this passage; this adds the colouring.

evidence.title: Bourgeois 1786: the plates, and a begun colouring
evidence.excerpt_other: l'autre avoit commencé à mettre en couleur la première planche, mais il tomba malade et n'acheva pas. J'ai mis son esquisse, toute imparfaite qu'elle est, dans la caisse
evidence.summary: Bourgeois sends the twenty plates to Delatour, with a coloured sketch begun by a pupil of Castiglione of the first plate. Delatour's note: only a small part on the left is coloured enough to read. WISH: where this coloured sketch went: it would be the only period colour source for a building.

evidence.title: Bourgeois 1786: fountains only here, and a throne in each house
evidence.excerpt_other: C'est dans ce quartier seul que l'on voit des jets d'eau, des gerbes, des cascades, des nappes, etc. ailleurs il n'y en a pas.
evidence.summary: Bourgeois: jets exist only in this quarter of the garden. Each European house has a throne. The houses have only 'alleged' European ornament, to show the costume.

evidence.title: Bourgeois: each European house has a throne, and 'prétendus' ornaments
evidence.excerpt_other: Ces maisons européennes n'ont que des ornements (prétendus) européens, pour en montrer le costume.
evidence.summary: An outsider's opinion of the ornaments, and a key point for Q59: a Jesuit of the day calls the ornament only 'so-called' European.

evidence.title: Delatour on the style: Italo-Gothico-Chinois
evidence.excerpt_other: le seul nom qu'on puisse lui donner, c'est celui d'Italo-Gothico-Chinois. C'est de l'Italien, de la fin du XVIIe siècle, et du commencement du XVIIIe siècle, tel qu'on le voit dans Borromini, Guarini, Bibiena
evidence.summary: Earliest source of the Borromini comparison. Reads as a judgement of style from the plates, by a man who never saw them standing. Same note: stairs like Saint-Cloud's cascade and the Versailles ramp from the Fontaine du Dragon; perron like Caprarola. All likeness, none a stated model.

evidence.title: Test of the claim that the fountains stopped when Benoist died in 1774
evidence.summary: Result: the common form of the claim is wrong in two ways. (1) The machines failed before Benoist died: the wheel broke in 1763 and windlasses replaced it. (2) The fountains did not stop: reports of 1786 and 1789 have men filling the reservoir a day or two before a visit so that the water could play for the emperor (Bourgeois); wicker buckets from the river (Amiot); pipes repaired 1794, Dutch envoys meant to see the 水法 in early 1795 (E0185); machines scrapped 1795, but 嘉庆's poems of 1796-98 still mention water sent by machine: poetry, weak. Holding: after 1763 or so the fountains ran on occasion with stored water, carried by labour.

evidence.title: Q59: what Rabreau and Droguet add on models
evidence.summary: Nothing here proves a print filiation, so Q59 stands. In favour of print use: the Beijing libraries held the Cabinet du Roi plates and Pozzo's treatise, which Castiglione is said to have translated (his own claim), and Rabreau sets a Pozzo capital next to the plates, Droguet a Dal Re view of a villa theatre (1743) next to the perspective walls, with Fischer von Erlach and Kleiner in notes. Against a simple filiation: every one is an analogy, by Droguet's own method; Rabreau points out that the Dal Re view has clipped hedges and an arcade screen, not painted walls; he finds no ground for Beurdeley's Trianon or Fontainebleau. Period voices: Delatour's Borromini is style talk from the plates. The Jesuit letters give no description of the buildings (Rabreau).

evidence.title: Benoist in his own words on 'mes ouvrages hydrauliques'
evidence.excerpt_other: Comme dans ce temps-là je fus appelé à la maison de plaisance où Sa Majesté passe l'été pour y faire construire différentes machines hydrauliques ... Lorsque dans la suite, mes ouvrages hydrauliques étant finis, je vins demeurer à Peking
evidence.summary: Benoist, in a letter on a convert. He lived in the garden for the machines and moved back to Beijing when they were finished. No technical content. Spelling normalised from the old long s. Who wrote this letter is my reading from its content (a Jesuit on the hydraulic works), so mark 'likely'. Benoist's letter of 16 Nov 1767 to Papillon d'Auteroche (S600 n.; Kansai paper) exists but its text was not read here.

evidence.title: V&A on the commission and on its album
evidence.summary: Commissioned 1783, printed by 1786; copies kept in the palace and 200 further sets given to relatives, high officials and guests. Its seals suggest the album was in China but not in the garden in 1860; bought from E. Parsons in 1883. No source given for 200.

evidence.title: 御製 題澤蘭堂
evidence.excerpt_zh:
題澤蘭堂
書堂號澤蘭樸斵謝青丹芸帙堪永日藤窻避薄寒蕪情報韶意水法列竒觀（堂北為西洋水法處盖縁乾隆十八年西洋博爾都噶里雅國）（來京朝貢聞彼處以水法為竒觀因念中國地大物博水法不過工巧之一端遂命住京之西洋人郎世寧造）（為此法俾來使至此瞻仰前嵗□咭唎國使臣等至京朝貢亦令閲看深為歎服昨冬廣東督臣長麟撫臣朱）（珪奏荷蘭國使臣嘚□等以今嵗為朕御極六十年大慶懇請来京朝賀鑒其數萬里外慕化悃誠因允其請）（已即於臈月到京新正並與朝賀宴賞節間令於是處觀看水法使知朕所嘉者逺人嚮化之誠若其任土作）（貢則中國之大何竒不有初不以為貴也）洋使賀正至逺瀛合俾看
evidence.summary: The one imperial statement found on the European water works. Qianlong's note says the 西洋水法 stands north of 澤蘭堂; after a Portuguese embassy of 乾隆十八年 (1753) he had 郎世寧 Castiglione build it to show envoys; British envoys saw it in the 1790s, and the Dutch envoys at New Year 1795 were to see it. He adds that what he values is their coming, not their marvels.

evidence.title: Van Braam 1795, and Roux: the European buildings seen only as engravings
evidence.locator: via van Braam, Authentic Account vol.2 pp.?, IA authenticaccount02vanb OCR lines 1771, 2665
evidence.excerpt_other: He told us that the plan of them had been designed by Father Benoit, a French Missionary in quality of architect ; and that they had been built under his direction.
evidence.summary: Van Braam asked to see the European buildings and was told they were occupied by the Emperor's wives, so impossible; he had copies from the plates. Roux's word gives the plan to Benoist. This is a late attribution, against Delatour's Castiglione: note both. Note van Braam's 'occupied' is against Choutzé's 'never lived in'.

evidence.title: Delatour on 海晏堂's jets, compared with Saint-Cloud and Versailles
evidence.excerpt_other: Ils produisent le même effet que les jets d'eau qui bordent la cascade de Saint-Cloud, ou ceux du perron qui, à Versailles, conduit de la fontaine du dragon à la terrasse.
evidence.summary: The basis of the Versailles comparisons. An effect, stated by a Paris reader of the plates. Same for Malone's 'buffets d'eaux' from Lettres édifiantes xxiv p.421, which is a Jesuit's own likeness. Both are comparisons of effect, never a statement that it was the model.

evidence.title: Lucy: a 'Palais Louis XV' on about 8 October 1860
evidence.locator: letter of 8 October; IA OCR line 4098, page not fixed
evidence.excerpt_other: Nous dénichons aussi un Palais Louis XV. Il y avait là le matin encore les tapisseries des Gobelins, représentant la toilette chinoise, l'arrivée des Européens en Chine, etc., etc., présent du roi Louis XV à l'Empereur ... mais elles ont été mises en sûreté !! Plus loin, c'est une collection de portraits des beautés de la cour de Louis XV, avec les noms au bas. Crevés hélas !
evidence.summary: Witness of 1860: the French enter a European-style building, with Gobelins tapestries (the man names the wrong Chinese emperor) and pictures of court ladies with their names. Tapestries gone by the afternoon. Agrees with the plate XIV note and with S245.

evidence.title: Varin: chambers of Gobelins and portraits in a Louis XV palace, 1860
evidence.locator: IA OCR line 9748; S02 p.184 quotes it
evidence.excerpt_other: Dans un de ces palais, bâti dans le style Louis XV, on voyait une série de chambres revêtues de tapis des Gobelins aux armes de France, et aux murs desquelles étaient suspendus des portraits en pied de beautés de la cour de France, avec leurs noms au bas.
evidence.summary: Varin: secondary palaces, long abandoned and turned into stores. Tapestries and paintings 'delabrés, crevés': already in poor state. This is the same room as Lucy's. The two French witnesses tell us the building was a store with contents in October 1860, not an inhabited palace.

evidence.title: 王闓運 圓明園詞
evidence.locator: whole poem; copy without the 自注
evidence.excerpt_zh:
宜春苑中萤火飞，建章长乐柳十围。
离宫从来奉游豫，皇居那复在郊圻？
旧池澄绿流燕蓟，洗马高梁游牧地。
北藩本镇故元都，西山自拥兴王气。
九衢尘起暗连天，辰极星移北斗边。
沟洫填淤成斥卤，宫庭映带觅泉原。
渟泓稍见丹棱泮，陂陀先起畅春园。
畅春风光秀南苑，霓旌凤盖长游宴。
地灵不惜瓮山湖，天题更创圆明殿。
圆明始赐在潜龙，因回邸第作郊宫。
十八篱门随曲涧，七楹正殿倚乔松。
轩堂四十皆依水，山石参差尽亚风。
甘泉避暑因留跸，长杨扈从且弢弓。
纯皇缵业当全盛，江海无波待游幸。
行所留连赏四园，画师写放开双境。
谁道江南风景佳，移天缩地在君怀。
当时只拟成灵囿，小费何曾数露台。
殷勤毋佚箴骄念，岂意元皇失恭俭！
秋狝俄闻罢木兰，妖氛暗已传离坎。
吏治陵迟民困痛，长鲸跋浪海波枯。
始惊计吏忧财赋，欲卖行宫助转输。
沉吟五十年前事，厝火薪边然已至。
揭竿敢欲犯阿房，探丸早见诛文吏。
此时先帝见忧危，诏选三臣出视师。
宣室无人侍前席，郊坛有恨哭遗黎。
年年辇路看春草，处处伤心对花鸟。
玉女投壶强笑歌，金杯掷酒连昏晓。
四时景物爱郊居，玄冬入内望春初。
袅袅四春随凤辇，沉沉五夜递铜鱼。
内装颇学崔家髻，讽谏频除姜后珥。
玉路旋悲车毂鸣，金銮莫问残灯事。
鼎湖弓剑恨空还，郊垒风烟一炬间。
玉泉悲咽昆明塞，惟有铜犀守荆棘。
青芝岫里狐夜啼，绣漪桥下鱼空泣。
何人老监福园门，曾缀朝班奉至尊。
昔日暄阗厌朝贵，于今寂寞喜游人。
游人朝贵殊暄寂，偶来无复金闺客。
贤良门闭有残砖，光明殿毁寻颓壁。
文宗新构清辉堂，为近前湖纳晓光。
妖梦林神辞二品，佛城舍卫散诸方。
湖中蒲稗依依长，阶前蒿艾萧萧响。
枯树重抽盗作薪，游鳞暂跃惊逢网。
别有开云镂月台，太平三圣昔同来。
宁知乱竹侵苔落，不见春风泣露开。
平湖西去轩亭在，题壁银钩连倒薤。
金梯步步度莲花，绿窗处处留蠃黛。
当时仓卒动铃驼，守宫上直余嫔娥。
芦笳短吹随秋月，豆粥长饥望热河。
上东门开胡雏过，正有王公班道左。
敌兵未爇雍门荻，牧童已见骊山火。
应怜蓬岛一孤臣，欲持高洁比灵均。
丞相避兵生取节，徒人拒寇死当门。
即今福海冤如海，谁信神州尚有神！
百年成毁何匆促，四海荒残如在目。
丹城紫禁犹可归，岂闻江燕巢林木？
废宇倾基君好看，艰危始识中兴难。
已惩御史言修复，休遣中官织锦纨。
锦纨枉竭江南赋，鸳文龙爪新还故。
总饶结彩大宫门，何如旧日西湖路。
西湖地薄比郇瑕，武清暂住已倾家。
惟应鱼稻资民利，莫教莺柳斗宫花。
词臣讵解论都赋，挽辂难移幸雒车。
相如徒有上林颂，不遇良时空自嗟。
evidence.summary: A long lament on the garden's rise and destruction. It names the eighteen fence gates, the seven-bay main hall and forty halls by water, then the ruined 賢良門 and 光明殿, the new 清輝堂 of Xianfeng, 舍衛城, 鏤月開雲, and 福海 where the official 文豐 died.

evidence.title: 徐樹鈞 圓明園詞序
evidence.date: 1871 (同治十年立秋), recording a visit of 四月十日
evidence.excerpt_zh:
圆明园在京城西，出平则门三十里，畅春园北里许，世宗皇帝藩邸赐园也。圣祖常游豫西郊，次于丹棱沜，乐其川原，因明武清侯李伟清华园旧址，筑畅春园，藩邸赐园，故在其旁。雍正三年，乃大宫殿朝署之规以避暑听政，前临西山，环以西湖。湖水发源玉泉山，曰瓮山，度宫墙东流入清河，《水经注》所谓“蓟县西湖，绿水澄澹，燕之旧池”者也。东流为洗马沟，东南合高梁之水，故鱼稻饶衍，陂泉交绮。高宗皇帝嗣位，海宇殷阗，八方无事，每岁缔构，专饰园居。大驾南巡，流览湖山风景之胜，图画以归，若海宁安澜园、江宁瞻园、钱塘小有天园、吴县狮子林，皆仿其制，增制园中。列景四十，以四字题匾者为一胜区，一区之内，斋馆无数。复东拓长春，西辟清漪，离宫别馆，月榭风亭，属之西山，所费不计亿万。园地多明权珰别业，或传崇祯末，诸奄皆以珍宝窟宅于兹，乾隆间浚池，发金银数百万，时国运方兴，地不爱宝，上心悦豫，殚精构造，曲尽游观之妙，元明以来，未之闻也。每岁夏幸园中，冬初还宫，内廷大臣，赐第相望，文武侍从，并直园林，入直奏对，昕夕往来，络绎道路，历雍乾嘉道，百余年于兹矣。文宗初，粤寇踞金陵，盗贼蜂起，上初即位，求直言，得胜保、曾国藩、袁甲三三臣，既以塞 、程、徐、陆，先朝重望，相继倾覆，始擢用前言事者，各畀重任，三臣支柱，贼不犯畿。然迭胜迭败，东南数省，蹂躏无完土，上悯苍生之颠沛，慨左右之无人。九年冬，郊宿于斋宫，夜分痛哭，侍臣凄恻。大考翰詹，以宣室前席发题，忧心焦思，伤于祸乱，然后稍自抑解，寄于文酒。以宫中行止有节，尤喜园居，冬至入宫，初正即出。时园中传有四春之宠，皆汉女，分居亭馆，所谓杏花春、武陵春、牡丹春、海棠春者也。然上明于料兵，委权阃外，超次用人，海内称哲。而部寺诸臣，无所磨励，颇袭旧敝。晚得肃顺，敢言自任，故委以谋议。先是道光二十年，英吉利夷船，至广东香港，求通商不得，又以烧烟起衅，执政议和，予海关税银千八百万。英夷请立约，广督耆英，与期十年。届期而徐广缙督两广，夷使至广州，拒不许入，以受封爵，夷酋恨焉，志入广州。咸丰元 [ 九 ] 年，英吉利、法兰西、美利坚各国，乘粤寇鸱张，中国多故，复以轮舶直入大沽台。王僧格林沁，托团练之名，焚其二船，尽击走之。夷人知大皇帝无意于战，特臣民之私愤，乃潜至海岸，买马数千，募群盗为军，半年而成，再犯天津，称西洋马队，闻者恐栗，夷马步登岸，我未陈而敌骑长驱矣。十年六 [ 八 ] 月十六日，上方园居，闻夷骑至通州，仓卒率后嫔幸热河，道路初无供帐，途出密云，御食豆乳麦粥而已。十七日，英夷帅叩东便门，或有闭城者，闻炮而开，王公请和，和议将定。十九日，夷人至圆明园宫门，管园大臣文丰当门说止之，夷兵已去。文都统知奸民将起，环问守卫禁兵，无一在者，乃自索马还内，投福海死。奸人乘时纵火，入宫劫掠，夷人从之，各园皆火发，三昼夜不熄，非独我无官府诘问，夷帅亦不能知也。初英夷使臣巴夏里，已拘刑部，和议成，以礼释囚。于是巴夏里与英帅，各陈兵仗至礼部，订约五十七条，予以海关税银三千六百万，而夷人抵偿圆明园银二十万。王公奏言，未敢斥夷，文丰与主事惠丰，同死于园，不称殉节，但言遭兵燹而已。十一年七月，文宗晏驾热河，今上即位，奉两宫皇太后还京，垂帘十载，巨寇削平。而夷人通商江海，往来贸易，设通商王大臣，以接夷使。然常言：“某省士民毁天主教堂，某省不行其教，某省民教构衅。”日以难我，应之不暇，盖岌岌乎华夷杂处，又忽忽十有一年。园居荒墟，鞠为茂草，西山大寺，夷妇深居，予旅京师，恻然不敢过也。同治十年春，同年王壬父重至辇下，追话旧游，张子雨珊亦以计偕来，约访故宫，因驻守参将廖承恩许为道主。四月十日，命仆马同过绣漪桥，寻清漪园遗迹，颓垣断瓦，零乱榛芜，宫树苍苍，水鸣呜咽。由辇路登廓如亭，南望万寿山，但见牧童樵子，往来林莽间。暮从昆明湖归，桥上铜犀卧荆棘中，犀背御铭，琅然可诵。明日访守园者，得董监，自言：“年七十有余，自道光初入寺园中，今秩五品，居福园门旁。”导予等从瓦砾中，循出入贤良门而北，指勤政、光明、寿山、太和四殿遗址，前湖圆明寝殿五楹，后为奉三无私殿、九州清晏殿各七楹，坏壁犹立，拾级可寻。董监言：“东为天地一家春，后居也，西为乐安和，诸妃嫔贵人居也，洞天深处，皇子居也。清辉殿为文宗重建，与五福堂、镂月开云台、朗吟阁皆不可复识。”镂月开云者，即所谓牡丹春者也。世宗为皇子时，迎圣祖至赐园，而高宗年十二，以皇孙召侍左右，三天子福寿冠前古，集于一堂，高宗后制诗，尝夸乐之。经其废基，裴回惄焉。东渡湖，为苏堤、长春仙馆、藻园，又北为月地云居、舍卫城、日天琳宇、水木明瑟、濂溪乐处，仅约略指视所在。东北至香雪廊，阶前茅荻萧萧，废池可辩，有老监奉茶自石畔出，讶客所从来，颇似桃源人逢渔郎也。渡桥循福海西行，为平湖秋月，水光溶溶，一泻千顷。望蓬岛瑶台，岛上殿宇，犹存数楹，惜无方舟不达。其下流水潺湲，激石成响，董监示予：“此管园大臣文公死所也。”西北至双鹤斋，又西过规月桥，登绮吟堂，经采芝径，折而东，仍出双鹤斋。园中残毁几遍，独存此为劫灰之余，乱草侵阶，窗棂宛在，尤动人禾黍悲耳。双鹤斋西，为溪月松风，翠柏苍藤，沿流覆道，斜日在林，有老宫人驱羊豕下来。东过碧桐书院，地跨池上，东为金鳌，西为玉蝀，坊楔犹存。又东去，皆败坏难寻，遂不复往。莫色沈沈，栖乌乱飞，揖董监，出福园门，还于廖宅。廖，沣州人，字枫亭，少从塞尚阿、僧格林沁军，亦能言行间事，感予来游，颇尽宾主之欢。既夕言归，则礼部放榜日也。雨珊既落第南去，予与壬父每相过从，念言园游，辄惘惘不自得。壬父又曰：“园之盛时，纯皇勒记，必殷殷踵事之戒，然仁宗始罢南幸，宣宗尤忧国贫，秋狝之礼，辍而不举。惟夫张弛之道宜及，嘉道时，补纯皇倦勤之功，而内外大臣，惟务慎节，监司宽厚，牧令昏庸，讳盗容奸，以为安静。八卦妖徒，连兵十载，无生天主，教目滋繁，由游民轻法，刑废不用故也。江淮行宫，既皆斥卖，国之所患，岂在乏财。”又曰：“燕地经安史戎马之迹，爰及辽金，近沙漠之风矣。明太宗以燕王旧居，不务改宅，仍而至今，地利竭矣。又园居单外，非所以驻万乘，废而不居，盖亦时宜。”
予曰：“然，前年御史德泰，请按户亩鳞次捐输，复修园宫。大臣以侈端将启，请旨切责，谪戍未行，愤悔自死。自此莫敢言园居者。而比年备办大婚，费已千万，结彩宫门，至十余万，公奏朝廷动用钱粮，婚以成礼，岂在华饰，若前明户部司官得以谏争，予且建言矣。又予闻慈安太后在文宗时，有脱簪之谏，《关雎》《车舝》之贤，中兴之由也。又园宫未焚前一岁，妖言传上坐寝殿，见白须老翁，自称园神，请辞而去，上梦中加神二品阶，明日，至祠谕祀之，未一期而园毁，岂能定欤？子能诗者，达于政事，曷以风人之意，备《繁霜》《云汉》之采？”于是壬父为《圆明园词》一篇。而周学士（即大学士周祖培）、潘侍郎见之，并叹其伤心感人，笔墨通于情性。予以此诗可传后来，虑夫代远年逝，传闻失实，词中所述，罔有征者，乃为文以序之。同治十年立秋日，长沙徐树钧撰。
evidence.summary: A walk through the ruins eleven years after the destruction, guided by an old eunuch who had served since the 1820s. It says which sites could still be read, and that 雙鶴齋 with its surroundings alone stood, as did some rooms on 蓬島瑶臺 and the 金鼇 and 玉蝀 arches. Its account of 1860 credits the first fires to local robbers, which differs from the British and French record in S02.

evidence.title: 玉明 侍游御園記 (in 蕉軒隨錄)
evidence.locator: 蕉軒隨錄, 御園侍游 (line 336 of the corpus file)
evidence.excerpt_zh: ◎御园侍游玉将军（明）有《侍游御园记》，成竹坪同年（林）曾属予代作跋语，恭书于后。按，《记》云：“咸丰六年秋七月二十一日，奉旨：本日散朝后，著玉明、肃顺自备鞍马，午初一刻进西南门，在山高水长伺候。有顷，上从内乘船，至山高水长后阁扇下船，出前门，谕玉明、肃顺暨珠勒亨、西拉布、托云、德勒格尔、伊勒东阿等脱去外褂。上乘马，命七臣随行。自山高水长游藻园，至厂地，过汇芳书院，复由紫碧山房至鱼跃鸢飞少坐。过蕊珠宫门，至黄花磴进茶毕，往西洋楼海宴堂，至转马台，过小角门，至狮子林清淑斋赏饭。左右四卓，命七臣坐，并奉温谕可饱食，非外边筵宴比也。上命膳房先给七臣面各一器，上进面，复进饭，颁赏御用菜蔬，七臣叩头谢。上进粥，复赏粥毕。随驾起行，由宝相寺、法慧寺、谐奇趣过明春门，至雷峰夕照马头，坐如在天上船，游福海。上命笔砚作诗毕，至渊氵亭镜澈马头下船。进丽春门骑马，由旧园东墙根过敷春堂，游西大堤汉城关，至含辉楼下马，命七臣散归。玉明自道光十一年由侍卫擢厕御前二十余年，仰邀优渥，得遍瞻御园盛景。欣感之余，谨作记以纪荣遇。”
evidence.summary: A rare first-hand record of a day in the garden four years before its destruction. The emperor takes seven officials by a named route from 山高水長 through 藻園, 彚芳書院, 紫碧山房 and 魚躍鳶飛, past 蕊珠宫門, on to 海宴堂 in the 西洋樓, a meal at 清淑齋 in 獅子林, 寳相寺, 法慧寺, 諧奇趣, by boat on 福海, then 敷春堂 and 含暉楼. All were standing then.

evidence.summary: Gordon's letter of October 1860 with the order and the reason given by proclamation. S02 p.187 quotes the same letter.

evidence.title: Loch: reasons and notice
evidence.excerpt_other: that Yuen-Ming-Yuen would be burnt on the 18th, as a punishment inflicted on the Emperor for the violation of his word, and the act of treachery to a flag of truce ;
evidence.summary: Proclamation in Chinese posted on walls and buildings near the camps and the palace. Michel's division moved on Thursday 18 October. He repeats the estimate of over two hundred buildings on grounds of eight by ten miles.

evidence.title: Loch: what survived; passage likely on 清漪园
evidence.excerpt_other: indeed, only portions of the buildings themselves were burnt, and although the destruction, from the volumes of smoke, appeared immense, still a great portion escaped,
evidence.summary: A marble terrace along a lake three miles long and a bronze cow lying down: these details fit 清漪园 at 万寿山, not the Yuan Ming Yuan, though he uses that name. Do not place on our objects.

evidence.title: Lucy: French view of the burning
evidence.excerpt_other: Cet admirable palais , ou plutôt ces admirables palais, qui , bien que dépouillés de leurs richesses passées n en restaient pas moins une merveille , ne sont plus qu'un monceau de cendres.
evidence.summary: A French naval paymaster's letter: the English burned the remains on 18 October; Montauban did not join and protested. His earlier note of 7-8 October says fire by the Chinese. Date of the letter inferred from "hier 18 octobre".

evidence.title: M'Ghee: a hillside temple and a house on a terrace
evidence.excerpt_other: We ascended a flight of some seventy or eighty marble steps, a gentle stream of water at each side falling into a large marble basin at the bottom, bridged with marble also;
evidence.summary: A large circular temple with a triple gilded Buddha at the top of the steps, then along the terrace a house with ten or twenty rooms, in terraced courts on a hillside. Not identified: it may lie outside the three gardens.

evidence.title: Wolseley: 18-19 October 1860
evidence.excerpt_other: By the evening of the 19th October, the summer palaces had ceased to exist, and in their immediate vicinity, the very face of nature seemed changed : some blackened gables and piles of burnt timbers alone indicating where the royal palaces had stood.
evidence.summary: 1st division under Michel marched from the camp near Peking on 18 October and set fire to all the palaces. Smoke over Peking two days. Pines near buildings burned too. He says the French had looted all and destroyed some of the buildings, and objected to complete destruction.

evidence.title: Varin: behind the palace, and a European building with Gobelins
evidence.excerpt_other: Dans un de ces palais, bâti dans le style Louis XV, on voyait une série de chambres revêtues de tapis des Gobelins aux armes de France,
evidence.summary: Behind the palace a much larger lake with three buildings; then a maze of canals, lakes and hills with secondary palaces long abandoned and used as stores. The European one held Gobelins and portraits, in poor state. Building not named.

evidence.title: Hérisson: a rock mountain with a porcelain pagoda, and the imperial library (low trust)
evidence.excerpt_other: Son sommet est couronné par une petite pagode de huit mètres sur six de côté, surmontée de ses toits, entièrement construite en porcelaine blanche et jaune décorée d'étoiles. [...] C'est la Bibliothèque impériale. Son toit, en tuiles jaunes, semblable à celui de la salle du Trône [...] La salle a douze mètres de haut, dix de large et quarante de longueur.
evidence.summary: Hérisson describes a rock mountain dominating the park, topped by an 8 x 6 m pagoda of white and yellow porcelain to Guanyin, and to its right a yellow-tiled imperial library 12 m high, 10 m wide and 40 m long with shelves of manuscripts and two small altars. Malone calls him the least reliable account (S246 note); the sizes do not fit 文源阁 as the texts give it, so the tie is a guess.

evidence.title: Rennie: orders to restore
evidence.excerpt_other: and orders have been issued for the restoration of Yuen-ming-yuen.
evidence.summary: Diary from Peking; his footnote says that by April 1862 no steps had been taken. Page from nearby running heads.

evidence.title: Victor Hugo to Captain Butler: the protest letter
evidence.excerpt_other: Un jour, deux bandits sont entrés dans le Palais d'été. L'un a pillé, l'autre a incendié.
evidence.summary: Hugo, who never saw the garden, condemns the expedition: the Summer Palace was to oriental art what the Parthenon is to ideal art; of the two victors one looted and the other burned, and he names Elgin. A moral witness, not a source for any form or place.

evidence.title: Favier: contents, and a count of fourteen palaces
evidence.excerpt_other: Rien ne peut donner une idée des merveilles entassées depuis plus de 200 ans dans les quatorze palais dont était composé le Yuen-ming-yuen ;
evidence.summary: Written 37 years later, from others. Fourteen palaces by his count, against forty (Grant) and two hundred (Attiret, Loch). Plates of the ruins on the facing pages.

evidence.title: Bushell: objects and glazed figures from the gardens
evidence.excerpt_other: brought from the summer palaces at Yuan Ming Yuan which were burned in 1860, such as large images of Kuan-Yin enamelled with turquoise blue and other soft colours posed on purple pedestals, smaller Buddhist images once built in the brick walls of temples,
evidence.summary: Glazed Guanyin figures, small Buddhas once set in temple walls, dragons, qilin, phoenixes, in European museums. V&A enamels with numbers: ice-chest, incense burner 257-'76, elephant 1660-82, box 917-73. Compound not known. Useful for glaze colours and wall niches only.

evidence.title: 16-18 October 1860: decision and order
evidence.excerpt_other: The funeral of the British prisoners took place in the Russian cemetery not far from the British headquarters on October 17th, and on the 18th, although the French refused to cooperate, General Grant sent a force of 3500 men under Sir John Michel to burn the Yuan Ming Yuan.
evidence.summary: Elgin's letter to Prince Gong of 16 October gave notice of destruction and demanded 300,000 taels for the prisoners' families. 26 British captured, 13 returned alive; 13 French, 5 alive (Morse). Malone reports the local tradition that the prisoners were held at the Chi Hsien Yuan (集贤院, my reading) north of Haidian, not in the Yuan Ming Yuan.

evidence.title: 18-19 October 1860: the burning
evidence.excerpt_other: The British troops burned libraries of choice and rare books, notably one of the four copies of the great compilation of Ch'ien Lung's day, the Ssu K'u Ch'uan Shu, temples, dwellings, Chinese and foreign halls, storerooms, pavilions, offices, and lastly the Main Audience Hall itself,
evidence.summary: From M'Ghee pp.283-89 and Gordon's letter (Boulger pp.45-46). Beyond the three gardens the fire reached 万寿山, 玉泉山 and 香山, because Yuan Ming Yuan meant the whole region to the British. A north-west wind carried the smoke over Peking. Destruction dated 18 and 19 October on p.189.

evidence.title: Father Bourgeois 1786 on the contents of the European palaces
evidence.excerpt_other: In the hall which he had made new for the tapestries of the manufacture of Gobelins, which the French court sent in 1767, there are many pier glasses.
evidence.summary: Bourgeois, quoted via Combaz and Delatour: only European furniture and ornaments; window panes cut from Venetian and French mirror glass; a new hall 70 ft long for the Gobelins tapestries sent in 1767, crowded with machines. Not named here; S258 p.183 ties the Gobelins building to plate XIV, 远瀛观. Benoist's pneumatic machine was also sent here (Lettres édifiantes xxxiii).

evidence.title: French presents seen in a European building, October 1860
evidence.excerpt_other: In one of the palaces built in the style of Louis XV, there were seen a series of chambers hung with Gobelin tapestries marked with the arms of France,
evidence.summary: Varin pp.240-44: Gobelins with the arms of France and full-length portraits of court ladies, dilapidated from years of neglect. Building not named; 远瀛观 by S258 p.183.

evidence.title: The Official Map (S01) as Malone describes it
evidence.excerpt_other: The only serious mistake in the Official Map which the writer has found is in the location of the Hsieh Ch'i Ch'u, the first building in the foreign group, which is about two inches too far to the south.
evidence.summary: Bought from the draftsman Pai's family in Haidian; scale about 1 to 1300; every gate, wall, road, bridge, hill, canal and bay. Pasted sheets show alterations, as at scene 40. Later than the album. Purely a ground plan. Already used in Q3, Q5.

evidence.title: Xiyang Lou: general style and the twenty engravings
evidence.excerpt_other: Ch'ien Lung's European palaces contained numerous false windows and doors, excessive ornamentation in carved stone, glazed tiles in startling color combinations, imitation shells and rock-work, meaningless pyramids, scrolls and foliage, and conspicuous outside staircases,
evidence.summary: Formal gardens, clipped trees, patterned paths, with Chinese rockeries beside. Malone had a set of the twenty copper engravings photographed in Peking, owned by Mr Wilfahrt, who bought them on the street in 1900 (n.15). He follows their numbering.

evidence.title: Xiyang Lou: origin, 1747
evidence.excerpt_other: The hydraulic machine and the first fountain were finished at the end of autumn.
evidence.summary: From the 1775 life of Benoist in Lettres édifiantes vol. xxiv: Qianlong saw a picture of a fountain in 1747, Benoist made a model, and the emperor resolved to build a European palace. Castiglione drew the plans with Benoist; Benoist designed the fountains and the "water castles" and trained the workmen. He worked on fountains for about twelve years. Which fountain came first is not stated.

evidence.title: Informants on the ruins: Lu, Ho, Tung
evidence.excerpt_other: He says he was twelve sui, or ten or eleven years of age, and employed there as a helper to sweep the walks and pull the weeds, when the palace was destroyed in 1860.
evidence.summary: Old Lu lived in a hut at the east end of 海晏堂, the source of Malone's oral details on the European buildings. The eunuchs Ho and Tung, still there in 1919, told him what was rebuilt after 1860 and destroyed again in 1900. Treat as oral: useful, unverified.

evidence.title: Delatour after Benoist: a throne hall inside
evidence.excerpt_other: ce perron élevé de quatre pieds au-dessus du niveau de la cour, est de plein pied avec le pavé de la salle,
evidence.summary: General, from Lettres édifiantes and manuscript letters of Benoist: covered porch 15 x 30 pieds on two rows of columns, 4 pieds above the court; doors 10 pieds high with solid lower 3 pieds and open carving above backed by paper; door curtains for winter, spring and summer. Which palace is not clear. Use for typology only.

evidence.title: Hérisson: a copy of the Nanjing tower and a 20 m bronze Buddha (low trust, place unsure)
evidence.excerpt_other: Un peu plus loin se dresse une tour, réduction exacte de la fameuse tour de Nan-Kin [...] La statue du dieu [...] n'a pas moins de vingt mètres de haut.
evidence.summary: A tower copying the Nanjing porcelain pagoda and a gilt bronze Buddha 20 m high in a pagoda built round it. Nothing in the scene texts of wave 1 matches; such a figure suggests 清漪园 or another garden, or invention. Recorded so nobody ties it later without care.

evidence.title: Differences between impressions: looked at 20 plates on 4 holders
evidence.locator: contact sheets in /opt/data/cache/scratch/palace_r6_tmp_plates/; plates 3, 8, 15 close up
evidence.summary: Same copper in all: on plates 3 and 15 the title, number, cloud bands and horizon match line for line; no re-engraved state seen, at these resolutions. Rylands is the darkest and crispest and keeps its margin and neat line, with a hand note 'Pl. N' top right and an Arabic or Roman number at the foot (S700 argues proofs). V&A keeps margins and neat line, printed lighter; red seals on the left margin; photographed open in the album. NYPL is trimmed to the neat line on a brown border, pale. Palace Museum is cut at or within the neat line, on patterned silk; plate 3's top neat line is gone. Measure from Rylands or V&A where the frame counts.

evidence.title: Order of plates in each set
evidence.locator: S700 canvases; S701 manifests; S74 accession numbers; S71 page list; S72 ss pages
evidence.summary: Getty and NYPL run 1-20. V&A 29452:1-19 runs 2-20, plate 1 missing. Rylands binds 二, the watercolour, 一, then 3-20. The Palace Museum web list is out of order (谐奇趣南面 and 海晏堂东面 near the end), so the Commons file suffixes do not give the plate number: -17 is plate 1, the unsuffixed file plate 2, -1 plate 3.

evidence.title: Zhang on the 20 engravings
evidence.summary: Sheets 88 x 51 cm. Bourgeois reported them finished in 1786 to the head of the printing house of the Bibliothèque nationale, after 大事记 1786 in 《圆明园》学刊 4 (1986) p.35. Authorship disputed: Chinese histories name Yi Lantai, one calls him Chinese, 大事记 a European; European sources mostly anonymous; Pirazzoli-t'Serstevens 1987 says Chinese pupils of Castiglione. 大事记 1786 also records a panorama of Changchun Yuan, now lost.

evidence.title: Garden of Perfect Brightness, MIT Visualizing Cultures, Lillian Li
evidence.summary: Teaching essays on the Forty Scenes, the European palaces with their 20 engravings, and the destruction and later photographs.

evidence.title: Garden of Perfect Brightness, MIT Visualizing Cultures, Lillian Li
evidence.summary: Teaching essays on the Forty Scenes, the European palaces with their 20 engravings, and the destruction and later photographs.

evidence.title: 三类 形制, 山墙 红色 (S47 section 3)
evidence.summary: S47 sorts the shrines in three types by form and notes that on the album the gable walls of seven of them are painted red, against grey or white on other buildings: 瑞应宫, 太岁坛, the 杏花春馆 earth shrine, the 北远山村 and 涵虚朗鉴 dragon shrines, 广育宫 and 多宝阁. A colour rule usable for the models.

evidence.title: 贾珺, 圆明三园中的祀庙祠宇建筑探析, 故宫博物院院刊 2012(3)
evidence.summary: A survey of the 33 shrines of the three gardens, with dates and forms: ancestor halls, flower god and dragon king temples, 河神庙, 关帝庙. The first thing to read for small temples with little else. Assigned here by type, not checked per temple.

evidence.title: 張恩蔭 清代文人筆記之圓明園文詞校正
evidence.summary: Modern article checking the Qing notebooks. It lists wrong names and places in 養吉齋叢錄 卷十八, and says that the author probably never entered the gardens. It also dates work at 接秀山房 (觀瀾堂) to 1817 and 澄心堂 in the 竹園 to 1814.

evidence.title: 刘阳, 《圆明园的故事》, excerpt on 西洋楼, 澎湃
evidence.summary: 刘阳: 海晏堂, 1759, largest of the group; behind it the water tower, an H-plan solid building with a gallery below and balconies above, and a spiral stone stair on the east.

evidence.title: 圆明园历史桥梁形制研究
evidence.summary: Park study of the forms of the garden's historic bridges, from archives and digs, intended to guide new bridges. Abstract on the page, the full text is an attached PDF.

evidence.title: 圆明园百景史事分景汇编
evidence.summary: Park compilation of recorded events scene by scene, from the veritable records, with a PDF attachment. Potentially the best single source of dated facts per scene. Only the opening read; see the wishlist.

evidence.title: 郭黛姮 lecture, 對圓明園古建筑的再認識, 人民网
evidence.summary: Lecture by the reconstruction's leader: Qianlong began 长春园 from 1745 for his retirement. A primer on what the team changed its mind about.

evidence.title: 圆明园围墙历史变迁考
evidence.summary: Park history of the walls and gates: loss from 1919 onward (army, road stone, sales), rebuilding from 1984 to 2006 on the old line. Historic gates include 明春门, 绿油门, 蕊珠门, 秀清村门, 藻园门, 福缘门.

evidence.title: The 'Summer Palace' Diaspora, Tythacott, SOAS
evidence.summary: Project tracing objects taken from the garden, now in British and French museums.

evidence.title: 圆明园工程则例、做法类文献档案; 圆明园档案目录索引; 圆明园研究专著、专文类文献 (1982年前)
evidence.summary: Three bibliographic lists of the archives, the building regulations such as 内廷圆明园内工诸作现行则例, and works up to 1982. Useful for finding what to request.

evidence.title: 圆明园西洋楼巴洛克艺术风格
evidence.summary: Reads Baroque ornament from Ohlmer's photographs of the 1870s and others of that period.

evidence.title: 圆明园西洋楼的中国元素
evidence.summary: Argues that the European palaces, designed by missionaries and built by Chinese workmen on imperial order, also carry Chinese traits in garden layout, building form and ornament.

evidence.title: 圆明园西洋楼的历史文化价值
evidence.summary: General account of the strip: begun 1747, mostly built by about 1759, with ten or more units in a band along the north wall.

evidence.title: 圆明园长春园西洋楼建筑是清代中西文化交流的产物吗？
evidence.summary: Questions the common praise of 西洋楼 as cultural exchange: it says the buildings were an imperial curiosity and had little influence. It gives the strip as about 750 x 70 m and the start as 1747, mostly complete by 1759.

evidence.title: 清代御苑胜境——圆明园西洋楼二十景图创作理路探赜
evidence.summary: On the 20 copper plates: how the Chinese artist 伊兰泰 Yi Lantai, long thought a Westerner, emerged from the archives after 1980, and what the plates' composition aims at. Gives 1783 and 远瀛观 as the end of building.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 西洋楼
evidence.summary: The editors walk the strip from west to east with completion dates and plaques: 谐奇趣 1751, 养雀笼 1759, then the fountains and the perspective walls, with their mechanical details. They put the whole at about 2% of the gardens.

evidence.title: Thiriez, Barbarian Lens: chapters on the group of photographs
evidence.date: 1998 per Hahn and Routledge; 1994 per UZH china-west record
evidence.locator: ch. 9 Ohlmer p.85; ch. 12 The Group of Photographs p.114; appendix 3 p.129, per the table of contents at e-aoi.uzh.ch/apps/china-west/documents/37941
evidence.summary: Would settle attribution among Child, Ohlmer, Piry, Moore and the numbers of each. Only the table of contents read.

evidence.title: 《圆明园 1707-1850 修建过程》
evidence.summary: Year-by-year building chronology citing the Imperial Household archives, including the 1831 rebuilding that produced Shende Tang.

evidence.title: The Garden of Perfect Brightness, A Life in Ruins, Barmé
evidence.summary: Standard English account of what became of the ruin after 1860. The link is the MIT reading list that cites it. Not read here.

evidence.title: A Paradise Lost, Young-tsu Wong
evidence.summary: Publisher calls it the first comprehensive study in a Western language. Not read here.

evidence.title: Liberal Barbarism, Erik Ringmar
evidence.summary: Studies the destruction of 1860 by British and French armies as ritual and as display of power. Summary from a catalogue, not read here.

evidence.title: 圆明三园进出水口探析, 中国园林 2024(4), 贾贯峰
evidence.summary: From Yangshi Lei plans: about 30 inlets and outlets. Main inflow by the sluice east of 藻园门; outflow by the sluice and 七孔闸 on the east wall of 长春园 and the two- and five-arch sluices on the east wall of 绮春园.

evidence.title: 《样式雷图上的春熙院》
evidence.summary: Argues from drawings for the position of Chunxi Yuan, north of Changchun Yuan and outside the three gardens.

evidence.title: 圆明园水利文物遗迹研究
evidence.summary: Inventory of water works: the 藻园 one-arch inlet, main source, now buried under the wall and undug; 黄花阵 inlet with good piers; 鉴碧亭 sluice, abandoned 2007; 狮子林 七孔闸, chief outlet, buried in the 2000s behind a new weir with only a stub showing; west water tower fed from a three-arch inlet.

evidence.title: 金勋 Jin Xun, plans and elevations of the European palaces, 1924, twelve published by Adam 1936
evidence.summary: Durand: Jin Xun's plans are drawn to scale, detailed, cover networks and paving, and for pipes at 海晏堂 and 谐奇趣's plan likely used originals; his paving agrees with paving on site in places. But no true measured survey: 90 m for the true 110 m at 大水法, stairs at 谐奇趣 unreachable, illogical wall layout at 线法墙. Answers point 2 of the brief.

evidence.title: 圆明园大墙丈尺及周边园林总平面图
evidence.date: 嘉庆十六年至道光七年 (1811-1827)
evidence.locator: 国家图书馆善本部 样式雷排架098-3号
evidence.summary: Plan of the outer walls with their lengths and the neighbouring gardens, 569x415 mm, ink, light colour, vermilion and red slips. No image here; the site may ask a small payment for the full record.

evidence.title: 圆明园来水河道全图
evidence.locator: 国家图书馆善本部 样038-1号
evidence.summary: Plan of the water supply and the country round the garden, 1128x699 mm, ink, light colour, red and yellow slips, presentation sheet, 1849: from the south wall of Yuanming Yuan to 清漪园, 昆明湖 and the 长河, neighbouring princely gardens, temples, villages, sluices and rice fields.

evidence.title: 圆明园、绮春园、长春园三园地盘河道全图
evidence.summary: Whole-garden survey for the Tongzhi repair; a check on every QC position, with the post-1860 caveat.

evidence.title: 《国家图书馆藏样式雷图档·圆明园卷初编》: 全图
evidence.date: mostly 道光, 咸丰, 同治 per the publisher
evidence.locator: 初编 目录: 全图, pp.1-12
evidence.summary: The printed facsimile of the National Library of China's Yangshi Lei sheets has a section on this place at pp.1-12 (12 pages, section length worked out from the next heading); sheet titles and numbers are in the volume, ordered from a library.

evidence.title: 圆明园附近河道全图
evidence.summary: Plan of the waterways around the garden with silt marks, cited in the printed volume's preface.

evidence.title: 圆明园周边水道图
evidence.summary: Daoguang-period plan of the waterways around the garden, cited in a paper on Chunxi Yuan as already marking that site a garrison; number not given.

evidence.title: 西洋楼水法图
evidence.locator: 国家图书馆善本部 none shown
evidence.summary: Plan of the Xiyang Lou waterworks across its dozen sites; the record shows no shelf number. No image here; the site may ask a small payment for the full record.

evidence.title: Three plans by Antoine Durand: 1984 from Jin Xun at 1/500 inside Adam's 1/10000; 1985 from a survey of the whole site; 1987 fountain area from 128 surveyed points with a manual survey of all surface parts
evidence.summary: The only published method statement for an on-site survey of the whole strip. Only excavation could fix the east fence of the gardens and the east edge of the basin. The west edge of the 线法山 gate and the ramp fix the geometry. See R0139-R0143. Plans without a printed scale in the copy I read.

evidence.title: Princeton's scrolls: what the holder says, against Malone
evidence.summary: The museum and the Tang Center catalogue an anonymous 1920s plan, ink and colour on three hanging scrolls, from Pai of Haidian through Malone to Bonhams 2016, Grindley and Princeton; no description, essay, bibliography or word on original or copy. Malone bought both a tracing and the original from Pai's side, and calls the original the Official Map. So the scrolls are one of those two, and the sources do not say which. No Bonhams lot page, nor any write-up by Liu or Kwok, was found. Q2 stays open.

evidence.title: 西洋楼区域考古勘探报告
evidence.locator: mhymy 档案史料 12205, free part
evidence.summary: Report's opening: the strip runs 860 m east-west, up to 300 m wide in the west and 65 m at its narrowest, about 70,000 m2, built 1747-1783. A central axis divides it into about five sections, each with its own north-south axis, thirteen units from 谐奇趣 to 线法墙. Survey results are paywalled.

evidence.title: 圆明园遗址的考古发现与认识
evidence.summary: Title of an overview by an archaeologist, seen in the index only. An important page to open by hand.
